1

Getting started

ChapterInstalling and first launch

Requirements

ComputerFormatNotes
Mac (Apple Silicon, Intel)AU, VST3Universal build. Also works in a DAW running under Rosetta.
Windows 10, 11 (64-bit)VST3Windows on ARM is not supported yet.

Installing on a Mac

  1. In the Finder, choose Go → Go to Folder… (⇧⌘G) and go to ~/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/Components.
  2. Put flipper.component in that folder. For a VST3 host, put flipper.vst3 in ~/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST3. You can install both.
  3. Restart your DAW.

The beta is not notarized by Apple, so macOS may block it the first time with an "unidentified developer" warning. Click Done in the warning, then click Open Anyway under System Settings → Privacy & Security, and restart the DAW. Do not click "Move to Trash".

Installing on Windows

  1. Right-click the downloaded zip, choose Properties, tick Unblock, then extract it.
  2. Put flipper.vst3 in C:\Program Files\Common Files\VST3.
  3. Click Rescan in your DAW's plug-in settings.

Opening it in a DAW Create an instrument track and choose tripper → flipper from the instrument list. If it is missing, rescan in the DAW's plug-in manager. Full install and uninstall notes are in INSTALL_mac.md and INSTALL_windows.md in the download.

The first screen An empty flipper shows two cards in the middle.

  • Drop a sample here to chop: drop an audio file to open it in the sampler, or click to choose a file.
  • Make a drum kit: click to open the drum screen. Drop several one-shots and they fill the cells from cell 1.

Three screens The switch in the header changes between the sampler | drum | fx screens. Changing screens does not change the sound or the MIDI key layout.

ScreenWhat it does
samplerChops one sample into slices and plays them on pads or keys.
drumPlays 16 one-shots placed in cells as a drum kit.
fxThe effect rack and the turntable deck. The sampler and drum output 1 go through this rack.
Story: how flipper came about
  • flipper started as a way to put the best parts of a few tools a sample-chopping producer used into one plug-in. The main wish was to have keep-tempo, pitch changes and the old-sampler sound all at once, live, on a single pad.
  • Its maker decided what to build and how it should sound; several AI (Claude) sessions wrote and tested the code on a Mac, a Windows PC and in the cloud.
  • An AI can't listen. So whenever a sound had to be chosen, a listening page with the candidates was made, and the maker's picks decided it.
  • At 0.7.0 the automatic tests were 970 self-tests, 381 engine tests and 25 tests each for VST3 and AU that open the built plug-in the way a DAW does.
  • Other companies' products were studied only through public documents and by measuring their sound; no code was taken apart.
In short
  • Mac: AU and VST3. Windows: VST3.
  • Open it from tripper → flipper in the instrument list.
  • Switch between the sampler, drum and fx screens in the header.

Header and basic controls

ChapterWhat every screen shares

No.NameWhat it does
1undo · redoSteps back, or redoes what was undone.
2flipThe name of the current work. Click the name for the flip menu (save, open, rename); ‹ › step through saved flips. An asterisk (*) after the name means there are unsaved changes. See chapter 8.
3screen switchChanges between the sampler, drum and fx screens.
4engineThe machine the sampler's sound goes through (clean, grey, black, purple). See chapter 3.
5visualizerMoves with every that plays. Click it for another look (paper confetti, plucked strings, a koi pond, marbled ink).
6volumeThe level of flipper's output, with a meter.

8settingsOpens the settings window. See chapter 7.
9day · nightSwitches between light and dark colours.
10stop allStops every sound at once.

Reading the meter The top bar is the left channel, the bottom bar the right. The scale holds the loudest moment briefly. The red mark growing from the right end is how much the is taking off. The dot at the end lights when the sound touches the top (0 ); click it to clear it. Drag the handle to change the volume (Shift: fine), double-click for 0 dB, or click the number to type a value.

Footer On the left is the credit, in the middle the current engine's name, and on the right the report a bug key.

Mouse and keys The same on every screen.

TargetActionResult
knobdrag up or downChanges the value.
knobShift + dragChanges the value finely.
knobdouble-click, Alt-click, Cmd-clickBack to the default.
knobclick the numberType a value. Click outside the field to finish.
knob, switch, keyright-clickOpens the MIDI learn menu (chapter 6).
any controlpoint at it with help onShows that control's tip.

Skins The look follows the engine: clean, grey, black or purple. Skins differ only in colour and material; every control keeps the same place and name. Under skin in the settings, pick clean, grey, black or purple to keep that look whatever the engine plays: grey's look with black's sound, say. Each engine's own options (black's filter, grey's drive, purple's clarity) stay with the engine and are drawn in the current skin.

Story: why the look follows the engine
  • Pick an engine and the window turns into that machine too. When only the sound changes, it's easy to forget which machine you are hearing.
  • With four skins, the same control started to look a little different from skin to skin. So before release came a rule: skins differ only in colour and material, and a control keeps its place, size, words and behaviour. A test now lays the four skins by side and checks it.
  • The header's visualiser was first called "the pond". Paper, strings, koi and ink looks were drawn and tried; the koi pond is still one of the looks.
In short
  • The header holds undo, the flip, the screen switch, the engine, volume, help and settings.
  • Drag knobs, Shift for fine moves, double-click for the default.
  • Right-click a control for MIDI learn.

Sampler

ChapterThe screen for chopping and playing a sample

No.AreaWhat it does
1sample rowopen, record, sample type, original tempo, mode, key, speed
2chop barchop method (auto, grid, lazy), sensitivity, gain, whole-sample keys, channels, detected key
3waveformthe whole sample with markers, start (S) and end (E)
4slice drawerstart, end, pitch, volume, fades, reverse and skip of the picked slice or all slices
5play rowplay as, pages, chop to MIDI, voices, pad plays
6padsOne slice per pad. A pad shows its number, MIDI note and any changed values.

Loading a sample

  • Drop a file on the screen, or choose one with the folder key (open) in the sample row.
  • Reads WAV, AIFF, FLAC, MP3 and OGG. m4a and caf open on the Mac only.
  • Files longer than 10 minutes cannot be loaded.
  • The sample is saved inside the project, so the project still opens if the original file is moved or deleted.

Sample row

No.NameWhat it does
1openChooses the audio file to chop.
2record a takeOpens the recording window. See "Recording" below.
3sample nameFile name, length and sample rate.
4 · loopA loop has a tempo and can follow the DAW tempo. A one-shot has none.
5original tempoThe sample's own tempo, guessed from its name and length. Type over it if it is wrong. Click it for candidates (from the length, from the file name).
6mode changes pitch together with speed. moves key and speed separately.
7keyThe whole sample's pitch. Drag for semitones, Shift + drag for , double-click for 0. Click the number to type semitones and cents together, like -3 20.
8speed · tempoPlayback speed. In repitch, type a tempo and press Enter, and the key moves to match it.
9crispIn keep tempo, leaves the front of each hit unstretched. Turn it on for beats and drum loops, off for melodies, chords and voices. In repitch, this place holds use DAW tempo, which sets the speed that matches the DAW tempo.
10DAW tempoWhen on, the DAW tempo sets the speed. Only for a loop whose original tempo is known.

Recording

The red dot key in the sample row opens the recording window.

ItemChoices
from (another track) or flipper's output (what flipper plays now, to )
whennow or next bar (starts on the next downbeat while the DAW plays)
lengthuntil stopped, or 1, 2, 4 or 8 bars (at the DAW tempo)

When you stop, the recording becomes the new sample. If the current flip is unsaved, flipper asks first. One take lasts up to 2 minutes and is kept as a 24-bit WAV in recorded in the flipper folder (chapter 8). Recording on the drum screen goes into the picked cell. Nothing is recorded during an offline .

The side-chain input is off at first. Turn it on in the DAW and send the track you want to record to it. Until it is connected, the window says so and the record key waits. Chapter 9 explains how in each kind of DAW.

Chop bar

No.NameWhat it does
1auto · grid · lazyThe chop method. auto cuts at every hit, grid on every beat division, and lazy where you tap.
2sensitivityIn auto, how strong a hit must be to cut. Higher gives more slices. In grid, this place holds the division (1/4, 1/8 …).
3gainThe whole sample gain. It applies to every pad, the record and the preview, before the fx. Each slice's own volume is in the drawer.
4re-chopChops again with the method of the visible tab. Locked markers stay.
5diceChops anew with the same number of slices. Click to roll; drag further for wilder cuts (one pip: only the strongest hits, six: anywhere). Locked markers and skipped slices stay.
6previewPlays the whole file while held, at the whole sample gain.
7truncateKeeps only S to E and cuts the rest, so the project and flip get smaller.
8normalizeSets the whole sample gain so the loudest point between S and E reaches 0 .
9magnetA you move snaps to the nearest .
10channelsWhich channels you hear: stereo, left, right, , . Anything but stereo plays in mono. stereo view in this menu splits the waveform into left and right.
11slicesThe current number of slices.
12detected keyThe key from S to E, shown as recorded → now (like Am → Gm). Click for other candidates, set by hand, or detect again. How far it sits from standard pitch (A = 440 Hz) is shown in ct.

Lazy chop Start the lazy tab and the sample plays from S; slice 1 begins at the start point. Every pad or key you hit while it plays starts the next slice there. The cut snaps to the nearest hit, so you can be a little early or late. In the settings, lazy chop taps chooses any pad or key or the lit pad (only the next slice's pad).

Waveform

ActionResult
scroll or pinchzoom in and out
Shift + scrollmove sideways
double-click the scroll barshow the whole sample
double-clickadd a marker there; on a marker, remove it
drag a markermove it. Hold Alt to turn the magnet off while dragging.
Shift-click, Cmd-clickpick several markers. The delete key (⌫) removes the picked markers.
right-clickmenu: add a marker here, lock marker, range starts here, range ends here, skip this slice
dragscratches like a record

Start (S) and end (E) The part of the sample in use. Chopping, key detection, normalize and truncate all work inside this range. Drag the S and E handles above the waveform or use the right-click menu; range: the whole sample resets it.

Locking a marker A locked marker stays when you chop again.

Skip Right-click a slice and choose skip this slice: that part makes no sound and leaves the pads, and the pads after it move up one place. It shows hatched on the waveform; bring this slice back undoes it.

Following the When zoomed in, hitting a slice off screen makes the view follow the playback position. Scrolling, the wheel or a click stops it until the next hit. It can be turned off in the settings.

Engines

Click the engine chip in the header to open the list; the picked machine's settings appear at the bottom of the list. Engines work in both repitch and keep tempo. The footer shows the current engine's name.

EngineSoundSettings
cleanthe sample as it isnone
greyfirm and warm; late-80s 12-bit, 40 kHzdrive, record speed
blackrough and dark; late-80s 12-bit, 26 kHzfilter, drive, record speed, melody pitch
purplesoft and muffled; early-90s game console, 4-bit, 32 kHzclarity, record speed
  • grey's drive: the harder it is driven, the rougher the 12-bit steps.
  • black's drive: lower is rougher; higher runs hot and clips the peaks.
  • black's filter: none (outputs 7–8), bright (13.1 kHz, output 6), dark (7.9 kHz, output 3), moving (opens on each hit, then closes; outputs 1–2). Click bright or dark again for their second step (11.6 kHz, 9.6 kHz).
  • black's melody pitch: the real machine changes pitch only in coarse steps. exact keeps melodies in tune, like black keeps the machine's error, and black's range plays like the machine only within its pitch knob's reach (−8 to +7). Pads always use the machine's steps.
  • purple's clarity: the rate it holds the sample at: clear (32 kHz), normal (16 kHz), muffled (8 kHz).
  • record speed: copies the old trick of sampling a record at 45 or 78 and playing it back slower. The top end gets rougher; key and tempo stay.
Story: how the engines were built
  • grey and black follow two famous late-80s samplers, and purple follows an early-90s console's sound chip.
  • Matching the bits and the sample rate wasn't the whole job. How each machine changes pitch, how it stores samples, its different filter per output and its analogue output stage were all rebuilt from public material.
  • black's moving filter was worked out from the machine's schematic. It opens wide on each hit, closes a long way over about a tenth of a second, and ends near 780 Hz. The 13.1, 11.6, 9.6 and 7.9 kHz of bright and dark are also the schematic's per-output filter values.
  • purple's chip arithmetic (the 4-bit sample compression and the 4-point gaussian read) matches an open-source emulator's code bit for bit: 7,300 random cases, about 50 million samples, all identical. The muffled colour after it is a filter worked out from the console board's schematic.

Slice drawer

No.NameWhat it does
1slice N · allWhether the knobs change only the picked slice or all slices at once.
2startWhere the slice starts, in samples. The previous slice's end moves with it. Drag or use the wheel; Shift moves one sample at a time.
3endWhere the slice stops. The next slice stays put; slice end: link to next slice in the settings moves them together.
4pitchThe slice's pitch (semitones; Shift: cents).
5volumeThe slice's level.
6fade inOpens the start of the slice smoothly.
7fade outCloses the end of the slice smoothly. Use it to remove clicks at a cut.
8reversePlays the slice backwards. The pad gets a reverse mark.
9skipTakes the slice off the pads. The pads after it move up.

Picking several slices Shift-click a pad to pick a range, Cmd-click to add one at a time. Picking makes no sound, and the drawer's knobs move all picked slices by the same amount.

Play row and pads

No.NameWhat it does
1play aspads puts one slice on each pad; melody plays the picked slice across the keyboard.
2pagesChanges the set of pads when there are more slices than one page holds. Pads per page (16 or 32) is a setting.
3chop to MIDITurns the current chop into a MIDI clip. See below.
4voicesmono: a new hit cuts the previous sound. poly: sounds overlap.
5pad playswhile held stops when you let go. whole slice plays to the slice's end.

Pads Clicking a pad plays its slice and picks it. Pad 1 is C3 by default, and each next pad is a semitone higher. With pad notes: white keys only in the settings, pads sit on the white keys only (pad 1 = C3, pad 2 = D3 …). Pad colours are by sound or 16 colors in the settings.

Melody The picked slice is spread across the keyboard, a different pitch on every key. In melody, scale, octave and root appear. A scale (chromatic, major, minor, dorian, phrygian, mixolydian, harmonic minor, major pentatonic, minor pentatonic) puts only that key's notes on the keyboard. The root is the key that plays the slice at its own pitch. Drag along the on-screen keys to play a run, scroll to move sideways, and Cmd + scroll or pinch to zoom.

More ways to play, by keyswitch MIDI (chapter 6) also select scratch and fx keys. Scratch scratches the hit slice on the record (pick the pattern on the fx screen; right-click a pad for its own pattern). fx keys plays the 16 fx pads from pad 1's note up.

Chop to MIDI Drag this key onto a DAW track to drop the current chop in as a MIDI clip: every slice plays its pad note where it sat in the original loop. Click it to save a MIDI file instead.

In short
  • Drop a sample, chop it in the chop bar, play it on the pads.
  • Chopping and analysis happen only between start (S) and end (E).
  • slice N · all in the drawer changes one slice or all of them.

Drum

ChapterBuilding a kit from 16 one-shots

No.NameWhat it does
1cells16 of them; cell 1 is bottom left. A cell shows its number, MIDI note, file name, an engine dot, its and its output (like →3).
2preview and nameThe picked cell's number, note, and file name. ▶ plays it.
3select allPicks all 16 cells.
4load… · clearPuts a file in the cell, or empties it.
5truncate · normalizeKeeps only start–end, or brings the loudest point between start and end to 0 dB.
6cell waveformTrim the part in use with the handles at both ends.
7start · endStart and end of the part in use, in samples.
8volume · pan · pitchLevel, position and pitch (±24 semitones). Pan is a stereo balance: turned fully to one , the other side of a stereo sample disappears.
9engineclean, grey, black, purple: the sampler's engines, chosen per cell.
10choke groupnone, 1–4. Hitting a cell stops the previous sound of the same group.
11fade in · fade outThe start and end of the cell's sound.
12fxFilter, punch, distort, crush and tape per cell. Click a tile for its settings below.
13sendsHow much goes to the echo and the space. To save CPU there is one echo and one space, shared by every cell; they play on output 1.

Loading cells

  • Drop a file on a cell. Several files fill the cells from that one on.
  • Drag a cell onto another to move it; onto a cell that holds a sample, to swap them. Hold Alt to copy. Esc cancels.

Picking cells Clicking a cell plays it and picks it. Shift-click or Cmd-click picks several; dragging a control then moves all of them by the same amount, and typing a number sets them all to it. A cell you hit is picked on screen too (not while several are picked).

Right-click menu load, clear, output, choke group, save kit, open kit.

Hitting the same cell again overlaps the previous sound. Put the cell in a choke group to stop that.

Playing Drum cells play from C6 to D#7 by default. While any cell holds a sample, C1–D#2 on MIDI channel 10 also play cells 1–16, whatever screen is showing. Chapter 6 explains how to move the zones.

16 outputs Output 1 is the main output and goes through the fx rack. Outputs 2–16 skip the rack.

  1. Insert flipper in the DAW as a instrument.
  2. Turn on inserted as multi-output in the settings or in a cell's output menu.
  3. Set the cell's output to 2–16 and route that DAW output to a mixer track.

A cell on an output the DAW has turned off plays on output 1. With the on, outputs 2–16 also stay under −0.3 .

Kit files Right-click a cell for save kit… and open kit…. A .flipkit file holds the cells' samples and settings. The default folder is kits in the flipper folder (chapter 8). Opening a kit in another project changes only the cells and leaves the sampler alone.

Importing other kits Drop these on the drum screen, or open them with open kit…:

  • a folder of audio files (in the order of the number at the start of each name, else by name)
  • an file
  • a single WAV of 16 slices (only when opened as a kit; a WAV dropped on a cell goes into that cell)
  • a kit from a Maschine library (expansion folder or .nicnt), or a .mxsnd
  • a program from an MPC expansion (.xpn)

Anything beyond 16 cells and built-in sounds without a sample are left out, and a layered pad keeps only its loudest layer. flipper tells you what was left out after the import.

Exporting a kit WAV kit for Logic · FL · Ableton… writes the cells as WAV files: as heard, as heard, with the echo and space, or the samples as they are.

In short
  • Put one-shots in the cells and play from C6, or from C1 on channel 10.
  • Cells in the same choke group cut each other.
  • Outputs 2–16 only work when the DAW inserts flipper as multi-output.

fx

ChapterThe effect rack and the turntable deck

No.AreaWhat it does
1rackTen effect slots.
2slot rowThe picked slot's controls.
3record stripThe work range on the record. Drag it to scratch. The deck's state shows top right.

Rack

The ten slots run in this order: filter, punch, distort (basics), crush, tape, chorus, noise (color), echo, space (space), master (end). The sampler and drum output 1 pass through them left to right.

  • Click a slot to show its controls in the row below.
  • Turn a slot's lamp off to take it out. Its values stay.
  • A slot whose knob is at 0 is off and costs no CPU.
  • The master's lamp turns the whole rack on and off; the slots look faded while it is off. The fx pads work even with the rack off.
SlotSlot knobSlot row
filterHigher makes it darker (LP), thinner (HP) or narrower (BP). All the way down it is open, the same as off.type (LP, BP, HP), slope (12 dB, 24 dB), , circuit (clean, ladder), place (first, end)
punchA : brings loud and quiet closer so hits come forward.mode (feedback, classic), snap, mix
distortBends the sound.type (soft, tube, fuzz, clip, fold), tone, focus, mix, flux
crushLowers the sample rate and bits.rate, bits, steps · smooth, mix, flux
tapeTape : the lows swell and the highs are pressed down.flux
chorusLayers a few slightly moving copies for width.speed, width, mix
noiseLays dust, hiss and crackle under the sound. Only while a sample plays; it fades within 0.15 s of stopping.type, tone, flux
echoRepeats in time with the DAW.mode (tape, digital, grain), time (sync or ms), repeats, tone, (digital), grain pitch and direction (grain)
space.type (room, hall, galaxy, light, tiny), decay, , stereo, flux
masterHow much of the rack you hear (0 %: the input as it is).input, width, output,

What each slot is built on Several slots use Airwindows plug-ins (by Chris Johnson, MIT licence) as they are; the rest were made for flipper. The number at the end of a plug-in's name is its version.

SlotTypeBuilt on
filterLP, BP, HPour own (clean: a state-variable filter, ladder: a saturating ladder)
punchfeedback, classicour own
distortsoft, tube, clipAirwindows PurestSaturation, Density3, ClipOnly3
distortfoldAirwindows Fracture2's folding curve (our own oversampling)
distortfuzzour own
crushrateAirwindows DeRez5 (the bits are our own)
tape–Airwindows ToTape9 (drive only, flutter off)
chorus–Airwindows ChorusEnsemble
noisedustAirwindows TapeDust
noisehiss, crackleour own
echotapeAirwindows TapeDelay2
echodigital, grainour own
spaceroom, hall, galaxy, light, tinyAirwindows kWoodRoom, kRockstar2, Galactic3, Ultralight2, VerbTiny (pre-delay and stereo are our own)
masterinputAirwindows ADClip9
masterwidthabove 100 % Airwindows SweetWide, below it our own /side

The Airwindows code comes from Airwindows Consolidated (commit 8a67b80), which gathers the plug-ins into one C++ library; only its MIT parts were taken, and the files are unchanged. Each plug-in draws its random numbers from a fixed starting value, so every sounds the same.

Story: how the rack's sounds were picked by ear
  • For each slot, several candidates were put on the same drum loop and keys loop on a listening page, and the maker picked over three rounds. The candidates were level-matched so that louder wouldn't just sound better.
  • For punch, a model fitted to a commercial sampler's compressor was compared with a simple compressor written first. On loops the simple one sounded better, so it stayed. The fitted model's long release seems to have held down the next hit.
  • Nothing among the fuzz and filter candidates fitted, so both were written from scratch.
  • The chorus slot was first called "wobble". Width turned out more useful than wobble, so it became chorus, and the tape slot's flutter stays off.
  • Noise only plays while a sample sounds because of a real mistake: a bounce with noise left on had hiss running to the end of the song.

Filter place first runs before every other slot; end runs after all of them, filtering the echo and space too.

Flux Makes the sound vary a little over time. It follows the DAW's beat, so a bounce sounds the same as what you heard.

Echo time sync is a beat length (. dotted, T triplet); ms is 1–2000 ms regardless of tempo. The shortest time is 20 ms for digital and grain, about 75 ms for tape.

Limiter The last stage before the volume. It works even with the rack off.

SettingWhat it does
safeCatches only what would go over −0.3 .
vintagePresses loud parts and rounds them off. Raise the master's input to push it harder.
offDoes nothing.

The limiter works on each output separately. Summing several outputs in the DAW can go over 0 dBFS.

Story: a sudden loud sound is the worst bug
  • During development, loading an old kit could make the sound jump +29 dB for an instant. That can hurt speakers and ears, so since then a sudden loud sound counts as the most serious kind of bug.
  • Every place that could make one (queued events released at once, echo and reverb feedback, a filter running away, loading a state, changing the sample rate or buffer size) has a test that checks the peak stays under a limit.
  • If a number breaks during processing (NaN, Inf), that block goes out silent and its cause is reset.

Deck

No.NameWhat it does
1platterThe record strip's work range becomes a record. Playing spins it at 33⅓ rpm; turning it with the mouse scratches.
2▶ · ■Spins and stops the record from the needle. It spins even with the DAW stopped, in the current mode and engine.
3record holdWhile held, the record and the pads slow down and stop as if held by hand. Let go and it spins again.
4repeatWhile held, repeats the sound at the length under your finger (1 bar at the left end to 1/64 at the right). Slide while holding to change it at once; let go and playback carries on. The 3 key on the right makes it .
5filterWhile held: open in the middle, closing the to the left and the to the right. Let go and it opens again.
6fx padsChange the sound while held. See below.
7faderHow much of the record you hear; the left end (turntable side) is open. cut closes the fader while held. curve is smooth (for mixing) or sharp (for scratching: a small move opens it fully).
8scratch patternHow the record is scratched. See below.
9pad pressWhether fx pads act while held or latch (press on, press again off).
10kicks inWhether repeat and tape pads start now or wait for the next 1/16 or beat.
11DAW starts · DAW stopsHow the record starts and stops while following the song. slow takes about half a second, like switching a turntable on or off; now starts on the beat or stops on the spot.
12follow the songInside a DAW only. When on, the record spins from the cue whenever the DAW plays and follows the song's beat.
13set cue · back to cueSets the needle's place as the cue (where the record starts), or puts the needle back on the cue at once.

fx pads Eight are on the screen; with the cut, repeats and filter there are 16 for MIDI (chapter 6). Several can be held together, and among the tape pads the last one pressed wins.

ColourPadsWhat they do
tealstop, back, half, revStop like tape or a record, spin back, drop to half speed, play backwards.
purpleecho, crushSend to the echo, or crush, while held.
greenchirp, babyScratch the slice on the record with that pattern.

Scratch patterns baby, chirp, trans and flare are shown; more holds all eight, adding forward, tear, 2-click and crab. In more you also set the length of one push and pull (1/2 beat to 1 bar) and a pattern of its own for the slice on the record.

  • hear: scratches the slice on the record with the picked pattern while held.
  • play it on the keyboard (in more): 16 keys in a row (C-1–D#0 by default) play slices 1–16. While held, a key puts its slice on the record and scratches it over and over; the hardest hit pushes the pattern's full distance and the softest 30 % of it. The setting applies first (with always full, every hit pushes all the way). on | off turns it on and off, and start moves the first key (‹ › one key, Shift an octave).
  • Every pattern starts on the DAW's next 16th note, or at once when the DAW is stopped.

Following the song When your hand, a pattern or the hold takes the record off the song for a moment, it returns to the song's place once it is back at speed. Grabbing the record or moving the fader while it follows can be written as DAW (touch, latch) and edited later. Turned off, the record spins only with ▶ ■.

Deck state The record strip shows the record's state at its top right: following the DAW, spinning on ▶, off the song for a moment, the pattern's name, holding, scratching by hand, spinning up, slowing down, stopped. Before the record has ever been turned, it shows "← scratch →".

In short
  • The rack has ten slots; a lamp takes one out, and a knob at 0 turns it off.
  • The safe limiter keeps every output under −0.3 dBFS.
  • The deck's record, fader, strips, fx pads and scratch patterns can all be played from MIDI.
6

MIDI

ChapterKey layout and MIDI learn

Default key layout

The same keys make the same sounds whatever screen is showing.

KeysWhat they do
C-2 · C#-2 · D-2 · D#-2: play as pads, melody, scratch or fx keys. They make no sound.
C-1–D#0Scratch zone: puts slices 1–16 on the record and scratches them with the pattern.
C1–D#2the 16 fx pads
C3 upsampler pads (pad 1 = C3)
C6–D#7drum cells 1–16 (while a cell holds a sample)
C1–D#2 on channel 10drum cells 1–16 (while a cell holds a sample)

The notes of the 16 fx pads (default, fx pads from C1)

Notefx pad
C1 · C#1 · D1 · D#1repeat 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16
E1repeat 1/32
F1cut
F#1 · G1filter (, half pressed)
G#1 · A1 · A#1 · B1stop, back, half, rev
C2 · C#2 · D2 · D#2echo, crush, chirp, baby

On a 4 × 4 pad grid they sit four to a row. From the bottom row: four repeats; 1/32, cut and the two filters; the four tape pads; echo, crush, chirp and baby.

While a drum cell holds a sample, the sampler pads skip the drum zone: pads 1–36 sit on C3–B5, 37–52 on E7–G8, and 53 on are played with the mouse only. With every cell empty, the keys above C6 are sampler pads too.

Moving the zones In the settings you can change the start note of sampler pad 1, drum cell 1, the fx pads, the scratch zone and the keyswitches. Click listen beside one and the next note you play becomes its start. When two zones share keys a red mark appears, and the one earlier in this list plays:

  1. MIDI learn
  2. channel 10 drums
  3. keyswitches
  4. scratch zone
  5. fx pads
  6. drum cells (while they hold samples)
  7. sampler pads

New flipper's keys Choose sampler first (sampler C3, drums C6) or drums first (drums C3, sampler C6). This applies only to newly inserted flippers; a saved project keeps its own layout.

fx and scratch zones in melody What the low keys do in melody: keep leaves the fx pads and scratch zone in place; give to melody makes every note play the melody, and the fx pads then listen on channel 16 only.

MIDI learn

Right-click a knob, switch, key or picker, choose MIDI learn, then move a knob or hit a pad on your controller.

  • forget: removes the binding. The menu shows what is bound (for example 20).
  • learn one more: the platter and the record hold can take several controllers.
  • while held · latch: for held controls such as the record hold, the strips and the fx pads, chosen in the menu after learning.
  • the knob sends: after learning a knob you can correct absolute or relative (endless encoder).
  • The platter can be learned to an endless knob, a touch strip, a pitch wheel or a pad.
  • Actions such as truncate, normalize, re-chop, dice and undo fire once per press.

MIDI in the settings

SettingWhat it does
MIDI knob pickupcatch when passing: the controller's knob moves the value only after passing it, so nothing jumps. jump: moves at once.
8 knobs in a rowClick learn 8 knobs, then turn your controller's knobs one by one from the left; they bind in a set order.
learned listEverything bound now; forget one or all.
save as defaultMIDI learn is saved per project. This makes new flippers on this computer start with the current bindings.

Notes learned for MIDI come before every key zone, and a learned note no longer plays a pad.

In short
  • Defaults: pads from C3, drums from C6, fx pads from C1, scratch from C-1.
  • Overlaps show red, and the zone earlier in the order plays.
  • Right-click → MIDI learn binds almost any control.

8

Files and saving

ChapterWhat is saved where

Projects Saving the DAW project stores flipper's sample, slices, settings, drum kit and MIDI learn inside it. It opens again even without the original files.

Flips (.flip) A flip is a file holding one flipper's whole work (sample, chop, settings, kit). Use it to move work to another project or send it to someone. Click the flip name in the header for its menu.

MenuWhat it does
save this flipSaves under the current name. With nothing changed, it reads "saved, nothing changed".
save as a new flip…Saves under a new name.
open a flip…Opens a saved flip. If the current flip has unsaved changes, flipper asks first.
rename · deleteA deleted flip goes to the trash.
open flip folderOpens flips in the flipper folder.

A flip made by a newer flipper does not open in an older one. Update flipper.

The flipper folder Recordings, flips and kits are all saved in the flipper folder. At first it is flipper in your Music folder; change it with flipper folder in the settings. The setting is shared by every flipper on this computer.

WhatIn the flipper folderMac defaultWindows default
flipsflips~/Music/flipper/flipsC:\Users\name\Music\flipper\flips
kitskits~/Music/flipper/kitsC:\Users\name\Music\flipper\kits
recordingsrecorded~/Music/flipper/recordedC:\Users\name\Music\flipper\recorded
copies of dropped filesdroppednoneC:\Users\name\Music\flipper\dropped
  • The setting is in the files section of the settings window. A folder picked with change… applies at once. back to default returns to flipper in your Music folder, and show in Finder (Windows: show in Explorer) opens it.
  • If the old folder holds files, flipper asks "Move the N files from the old folder to the new one?". They move only with move; with leave them they stay in the old folder.
  • A move never overwrites: when a name is taken, both are kept, the new one as name (2). If a file cannot move, the move stops there and names the file; that file and the rest stay in the old folder.
  • If the chosen folder's drive is not connected, flipper saves to the default folder until it can write there again. The setting stays, and the settings window says so.
  • A recording is saved in the flipper folder as it was when the recording started. The WAV kit export starts in the flipper folder's kits.
  • Samples are saved inside the project, so projects still open after the folder changes.
  • If you have moved your Music folder to another drive or to OneDrive, flipper uses that place.
  • Settings are kept apart from the flipper folder, in ~/Library/Application Support/tripper/flipper (Windows: %APPDATA%\tripper\flipper).

and performance An offline bounce sounds the same as what you heard live. Effects that vary over time, such as flux, follow the DAW's beat and come out the same too.

Update notice Once a day flipper checks whether a newer version is out and, if so, lights a small dot by its name. Click it for get it and stop telling me about this version. It sends nothing but the request itself. It can be turned off in the settings.

Reporting a bug Click report a bug at the bottom right to open the report window. Write what happened, what you expected, and whether it happens again, then send. The technical details sent with it are all shown before sending, and the report is anonymous and used only to fix bugs. Add an email only if you want a reply. After flipper closed unexpectedly, it asks whether to report it.

In short
  • Saving the project saves the sample with it.
  • A flip carries one piece of work somewhere else.
  • The update check runs once a day and sends nothing of yours.
9

Troubleshooting

ChapterCommon questions

There's no sound
  • Check the header's volume and meter. If the meter does not move, click a pad with the mouse.
  • With the fx rack's filter knob turned all the way up, almost everything is filtered out. Turn it down.
  • If only MIDI is silent, look for red marks on the key zones in the settings: the note may be taken by another zone or by MIDI learn.
  • Drum cells on outputs 2–16 are only heard once those outputs are routed in the DAW.
How do I turn on the side-chain input?
  • VST3 hosts with a -chain button above the plug-in window: turn it on, and in the sending track's sends or output choose "flipper - Side-Chain".
  • DAWs that route channels with a pin connector: send the track to flipper's track on channels 3/4, and connect 3/4 to the in the pin connector.
  • AU hosts with a Side Chain menu above the plug-in window: choose the sending track or bus in that menu.
Outputs 2–16 don't show in Logic
  • Insert the instrument as Multi Output (16×Stereo). A flipper inserted as stereo has only output 1.
  • In the mixer, add aux channels with the instrument channel's + key.
  • Turn on inserted as in flipper's settings.
The CPU load is high
  • calculates more than . Turning off high-quality in the settings makes it lighter.
  • Rack slots with their knob at 0 cost nothing.
  • Following the when zoomed redraws the screen more often. It can be turned off in the settings.
Do projects from older versions open?

Yes. Saved IDs and parameters stay the same across versions, so older projects and their open with the same sound. Kits made in the "flipper drum test" preview: save them as .flipkit in the preview, then open them in flipper.

OneDrive uploads my recordings

With OneDrive folder backup on, Windows keeps the Music folder inside OneDrive, so recordings and flips in the flipper folder sync too. Set flipper folder in the settings to a folder outside OneDrive (for example D:\flipper).

I'm worried about sudden loud sounds

With the on safe, no output goes over −0.3 . Start a session with the monitor volume low, and turn knobs that build up, such as echo repeats or filter , slowly.

Appendix

Default MIDI notes at a glance

KeysWhat they do
C-2–D#-2keyswitches
C-1–D#0scratch zone
C1–D#2fx pads (drum cells on channel 10)
C3 upsampler pads
C6–D#7drum cells

Every word in the pop-ups The notes behind the dotted underlined words, in alphabetical order.

automation Automation
The DAW recording and replaying parameter changes over time.
bounce Bounce
Rendering the song to an audio file in the DAW. An offline bounce runs faster than real time.
CC Control change
The MIDI message a knob or slider sends, with values 0–127.
cents Cent
A hundredth of a semitone, shown as ct.
choke group Choke group
A group whose sounds cut each other, like a closed hi-hat stopping an open one.
compressor Compressor
An effect that presses loud parts down to shrink the gap between loud and quiet.
cue Cue
The place where the record starts.
dBFS Decibels full scale
How far below the loudest level digital audio can hold (0 dBFS).
high-pass High-pass
A filter that lets only the highs through. Shown as HP.
keep tempo Keep tempo
Changing speed and pitch separately (time stretch).
keyswitches Keyswitch
A MIDI note that changes a setting without sounding. It can be written into a DAW track.
limiter Limiter
A last stage that keeps the level under a set ceiling.
low-pass Low-pass
A filter that lets only the lows through. Shown as LP.
marker Marker
A line showing where one slice ends and the next begins.
mid Mid
What the left and right share: the centre.
multi-output Multi-output
An instrument sending several outputs, each to its own mixer track in the DAW.
one-shot One-shot
A sound that plays once and ends. It has no tempo.
onset Onset
The moment a sound starts. auto chops at every onset.
ping-pong Ping-pong
An echo whose repeats alternate left and right.
playhead Playhead
The line that shows where playback is.
pre-delay Pre-delay
The gap between the sound and the start of its reverb.
repitch Repitch
Changing the read speed, so pitch and speed change together.
resample Resample
Recording flipper's own output to use as a new sample.
resonance Resonance
A boost around the filter cutoff. Turned high, it whistles.
reverb Reverb
An effect that makes the sound of a room or hall.
saturation Saturation
Rounding off the peaks the way tape or valves do when driven.
SFZ SFZ
An open instrument format that lists sample files and their key mapping as text.
side Side
Where left and right differ. The centre drops out.
side-chain input Side-chain input
A second input that lets another track feed the plug-in. Used for recording.
slice Slice
One part of the chopped sample. Each sits on one pad.
time stretch Time stretch
Changing length without pitch, or pitch without length.
triplets Triplet
A beat split into three, written like 1/8T.
velocity Velocity
How hard a key or pad is hit: 1–127 in MIDI.

Third-party code The code written for flipper is MIT; the plug-in as distributed bundles JUCE and Rubber Band, so it is AGPL-3.0.

CodeVersionUsed forLicence

Sound chip model–the purple engineISC

Story: how flipper is tested
  • A reference model written in Python is compared with the C++ engine, sound for sound.
  • The self-tests cover block sizes, sample rates, saving state, memory allocation, CPU, the screen layout, the Korean text and loud sounds.
  • The built VST3 and AU are opened the way a DAW does and checked for the same sound. 108 old projects, flips and kits from 0.2.6 on are checked to open with the same sound.
  • At any block size from 1 to 4096, live or offline, a bounce must sound exactly like what was played. No fix was allowed to break that.
  • Reviews were split into a side that hunts bugs and a side that tries to disprove them; outside AI reviews weren't taken on trust but reproduced one by one before fixing.
